note: A net with two continuous drivers - two devices sharing a bus. Used to fail, on hif-backend#88: the net regenerated as one `output reg` written by two always blocks, so the last process to run won and a bus driven by exactly one device read zzzz. The cause was in verilog2hif, which lowered every continuous assign to a process; it now keeps the continuous assigns of a net that two of them provably drive, and the regenerated module has the two `assign` lines of the source. Behavioral because the regenerated module kept the same ports and the same two expressions and reparsed cleanly; what it lost was that bus was a net, which no parse can check. replicated_z_literal covers one driver releasing a pin and the VHDL-sourced vhdl_shared_bus passes, so the gap was specific to the Verilog multi-driver path.
